justifications.1: Description names reviewing an expense or reimbursement claim against receipts and policy, with check/approve/audit triggers, and does not read as general accounting.
justifications.2: A full markdown template, a verdict table with approved-amount rules, and definitions of Basis, Questions and Summary make the four parts reproducible.
justifications.3: It states that writing the review is where the skill stops (no contacting the claimant, changing the claim or suggesting policy changes) and gives an explicit completion test.
justifications.4: Explicit rules cover no policy, no receipt, unreadable fields, no claim form, and receipt mismatches with the claimed line (needs information).
justifications.5: The policy is the only source of rules, embedded approval text is treated as a claimant assertion needing policy-specified evidence, and verdicts attach only to claimed items.
justifications.6: At about 1,200 words it is the longest, and the missing-input rules and uncommon cases (foreign currency, unitemised partial exclusions, form-total mismatches) sit ahead of and inside the common path.

justifications.1: Description targets reviewing an expense claim against receipts and policy with the specific verdict outputs, clearly not a general summarising skill.
justifications.2: The four parts are specified with table columns, total contents and sentence limits, and the three verdicts with approved-amount and citation rules are defined.
justifications.3: It defines when the review is done (every item has one verdict with evidence and the four parts are written) but does not say that no further action is expected.
justifications.4: A dedicated section handles no policy, no or partial receipts and no claim form, and unexplained receipt discrepancies become needs information.
justifications.5: Only the supplied policy and receipts count as evidence, authority claims in the material are content not direction, and unmatched receipts are never added to the claim.
justifications.6: At under 1,000 words the common path runs straight through four steps, with missing-input handling placed after them and whole-claim conditions handled in one short paragraph.

justifications.1: Description is specific to checking claimed line items against receipts and the supplied expense policy, with a use-when on supplying an expense claim.
justifications.2: Verdict definitions, an evidence rule and an output template with a reconciled total block define all four parts consistently.
justifications.3: Per-step done criteria are given, but there is no overall statement of what a finished review is or that no further work follows.
justifications.4: Missing inputs get only a blanket 'ask before starting', which conflicts with the needs-information rule for missing receipts; mismatched receipts are handled as needs information but a missing policy gets no partial-work path.
justifications.5: It confines rules to quotable policy clauses and verdicts to line items, but says nothing about treating approvals or instructions in the material as unverified content.
justifications.6: At about 800 words with short checklists that apply to every item, the structure is proportionate and uncommon cases do not crowd the path.

justifications.1: Description triggers on reviewing, checking, auditing or approving an expense claim or reimbursement request against policy and receipts.
justifications.2: Verdicts, the evidence format (clause plus deciding words plus receipt) and an output template with an example row define the four parts clearly.
justifications.3: A final pre-return check states what a finished review contains, but nothing says that no further work is expected after it.
justifications.4: A missing policy or claim form means ask and stop, a missing receipt is needs information, and a receipt that contradicts the claim is either rejected or needs information depending on whether a question could reconcile it.
justifications.5: The policy is the whole rulebook and silence means ask, but embedded approvals or instructions in the material are not addressed as non-evidence.
justifications.6: At about 760 words it is compact, with every rule on the main path and nothing rare given undue space.

justifications.1: Description is about reviewing an expense claim against receipts and a supplied policy for review or approval, not general accounting.
justifications.2: Verdicts, the three total figures, the questions and the summary are defined, with a template whose Evidence column specifies receipt and clause.
justifications.3: Step-level done conditions exist, but there is no overall completion statement and no instruction that the work ends with the review.
justifications.4: A missing claim form or policy means ask before starting, a missing receipt is handled line by line, and a receipt that contradicts the line is needs information.
justifications.5: Rules come only from quotable policy clauses and unmatched receipts are marked unclaimed, but claimed pre-approvals or instructions in the material are not explicitly treated as non-evidence.
justifications.6: The receipt checks that only some claims need (currency, tips, payer, duplicates) sit in a reference section after the steps, keeping the common path short.

justifications.1: Description triggers on reviewing an expense or reimbursement claim against receipts and policy and names the four outputs.
justifications.2: A template defines each part, including the Basis column for verdict grounds and the addition shown for the approved total.
justifications.3: It says the skill stops when the review is delivered, leaving approving, paying and contacting the claimant to the approver, and gives an explicit completion test.
justifications.4: Explicit rules cover no claim form, no policy (still run every step) and missing receipts, and receipt amounts that differ from the claim are recorded and decided.
justifications.5: Rules come only from the policy, facts only from receipts, embedded notes such as pre-approvals are content not direction, and unmatched receipts add nothing to the total.
justifications.6: At about 1,100 words, the missing-input and authority sections sit before the steps and an extra Other findings section is added, so the common path carries rarely needed material.
